note: Tahoe National Forest campground in cedar and pine on the north bank of the South Yuba River at I-80 exit 164 (Eagle Lakes Road), Cisco Grove; freeway noise carries. A swimming hole is beside the campground (fast, high water in early summer). The Indian Springs OHV staging area next door is the jumping-off point for the Fordyce 4x4 trail, so expect off-road traffic. Most lower-loop sites are short; the upper loop takes longer rigs. --Claude
summary: FS page + rec.gov facility/rates/catalog + imagery read. $24, extra vehicle $5; 34 sites (16 take 23 ft+, max 35), vault toilets + water, no hookups (confirmed); season ~05-21..10-15; reservable with 3 FCFS sites, 14-night max. OHV staging area adjacent (flag). Phone ''->530-288-3231; website forest root -> campground page. Not waterfront kept; rec.gov riverfront tags are a lead only.
flags: OHV (flag, keep): recreation.gov: 'The Indian Springs OHV Staging Area is adjacent to the campground and offers access to many OHV trails including the popular Fordyce 4x4 jeep trail.' The campground itself is a general riverside FS campground (reservable family sites, swimming hole); the staging area is a separate facility next door. Reads as a general campground with an OHV side: keep with an off-road-traffic caveat (written into the note).

FIT: FS says 'limited space for small trailers', but the rec.gov catalog posts 24-35 ft on the upper loop (15-28) plus 06 (23) and 14 (30): 16 of 34 sites take a 23-ft rig. Lower-loop sites 02-05 and 07-13 are 18-22 ft.

WATERFRONT LEAD (value not changed, 'not waterfront' kept): rec.gov tags 04 (22 ft, too short), 06 (23 ft) and walk-in tent sites 29-35 'Riverfront' and lists 'Waterfront Sites'. The South Yuba here is ~10-15 m wetted (creek-size), and on imagery the plotted sites sit ~50-70 m from the boulder channel under continuous canopy. Only 06 could be a creekside candidate, and it can't be shown over open ground; site photos would be needed.
